source_en: Locked the Rustaveli lot booth. Home.
Resident. Papers in my left pocket.
Done for the night. Going home.
Taking my wife to the anniversary opera.
Football training. Midfield on Sundays.
New in town. Seeking parking attendant work.
Papers. Here. Long shift. Three months through this checkpoint. Look it up.
Twenty-two years at that lot. Not once have I been late checking in.
Good. Another shift done, then. Thank you.
Four walls. At least it is warm. I have had worse.
You have a chair in there? My knee does not like standing.
Hm. Twenty-two years... and this is how it ends.
Not how I thought it would go. But. Alright.
Where are you coming from?
The lot on Rustaveli. Logged the last car, locked the booth. Going home.
The lot by the train station. Six years there now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My knee. It acts up this time of year. Nothing serious.
Nothing. Knees of a young man. I stand all day, no chair.
Twenty-two years at that lot and not one car stolen. Think about that.
This line moves slower than the lot on New Year's Eve.
What happened to the last officer?
Stopped coming. His car's still in my lot. I log it every day.
Which officer? I don't watch the checkpoint. The station lot keeps me busy.
